Processing overview

Audio processing, quality checks, and exploratory findings.

Abstract

I study how acoustic features and word choice relate to perceived stress, and whether these measures change after lifestyle interventions.

My work includes a local Python pipeline for acoustic feature extraction and Whisper transcription, quality checks, and analyses of study visits and stress questionnaires. I built the research dashboard to help the lab review processing coverage, flagged recordings, and saved results.

  • Before and after: The average acoustic score fell a little among 277 people with both visits. The differences between intervention and control groups were not statistically significant.
  • Reported stress: In the separate baseline analysis, higher acoustic scores went with slightly lower reported stress, opposite to the score’s intended direction. None of the separate age/sex-adjusted feature comparisons passed multiple-testing correction.

Interpretation: These results do not validate the current composite as a measure of stress. Further work needs to address feature definitions, score construction, and questionnaire timing.

This public summary contains real group-level statistics. Individual records, names, aliases, recordings, transcripts, source references, and participant exports are not included. The full research dashboard and repository remain private.
